text: Centre, in Imam Khomeini Hospital. Before the start of the study, all
patients in both groups had early stage invasive ductal carcinoma
BC (without metastasis). The mean age of treatment with M2000
was 45.2 ± 12.1, and the mean age of the non‐treatment group was
46.2 ± 10.8 years. All of the patients enrolled in this trial were female.
The oral administration of M2000, with a capsule of 500 mg, two
times daily (1000 mg/d), resulted in a partially positive response after
8 weeks of M2000 therapy. From 20 patients that consumed M2000,
one patient showed a decrease in mass size (5%), and in five patients, a
stopping of tumour growth (25%) was observed. In fourteen patients
(70%), although the size of the mass was higher than the starting point,
the growth rate was not statistically significant, as compared to the
non‐treatment group (Table 2). The evaluation of carcinoembryonic
antigen (CEA) and Cancer antigen 15‐3 (CA15‐3) showed that there
was no significant difference between treatment and non‐treatment
groups in this trial following M2000 therapy in pre‐surgical BC patients.
As shown in (Table 3), the M2000 therapy revealed an excellent
tolerability without any notable adverse effects during the study.
Laboratory tests showed no significant change after 8 weeks.
